C0.note: Computational complexity and experimental evaluation of ABC rules.

C1.quote: we ask for the complexity of computing election results
C1.note: NP-hardness results plus a simulation-based visualization on synthetic ideal points. Roughly equal; AL listed first.

C2.2.quote: We consider the approval preference model
C2.2.note: DICH only through the cited title 'Structure in dichotomous preferences'; input is approval sets.

C2.3.quote: the point xa describes a's ideal position
C2.3.note: Ideal points and radii are held positions that generate approval sets.

C2.4.quote: each voter specifies a subset of candidates that he or she finds suitable
C2.4.note: Approval sets are derived from ideal points and radii; rules applied directly; no statement on sincerity or reporting.

C3.2.note: No statement that voters submit their held attitude.

C4.1.note: The paper does not use utility, welfare, satisfaction or distortion for voters in a way that triggers applicability; the approval link is geometric. Mentions of 'satisfy the voters' are informal.

C4.2.note: Term 'dichotomous preferences' appears only in a cited title.

C5.1.note: Rules are evaluated experimentally on proportionality and diversity of the resulting committees across the space (e.g. asymmetric Gaussians 'highlight rules' abilities to choose proportional results').

C5.2.quote: one would expect a proportional rule to choose more candidates from there
C5.2.note: Evaluation is on the generated approval profiles and ideal point positions; no statement relating the input to a held attitude.

VOT.note: Voters are generated inputs only; they take no action in the model.

C8.1.note: NA: no type is STRAT or MIXED.

claims.quote: one should not force the voters to approve a fixed number of candidates
AV might have some deficiencies as a rule to choose individually excellent candidates

C9.1.note: Claims about which protocol or rule to use.

C9.2.note: Claims about quality of committees need that approval sets reflect voters' views, i.e. the input-held-attitude relation, and that Euclidean distance indicates desirability; the paper states the geometric generation but not an input-attitude relation, and results depend on the synthetic distributions.
